messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: apigw.latency spike and elevated 502/504 rate across eu-west edge (threshold breach). Incident ID INC-2026-0427. Paging @leah (on-call). Telemetry: https://grafana.redwood/in/edge/apigw?range=5m

leah: On it — joining call, will post quick triage. Anyone seeing customer-facing alerts?

kevin: Support channel reporting 3 customers with increased error rates on /v1/generate (EU). Escalating to AMs.

samir: Quick metrics: error rate went from ~0.3% -> 8.2% over 4m. 95th latency jumped from 180ms -> 1.1s. Top upstream: edge-mux-3 and edge-mux-7 have most 502s.

alex: Can we circuit some traffic off those mux pods? Suggest temp route exclude via quick traffic-shift to eu-west-2.

jordan: I can flip circuit breakers on mux-3/7. Doing a conservative 30% knockback to spare capacity for healthy pods. Will monitor.

jordan: Applied knockback via `kubectl patch svc edge-mux-3 -p '{"spec": {"externalTrafficPolicy": "Local"}}'` (manual flow control). Results incoming.

samir: After knockback (30s) error rate dropped to 4.1% and lat p95 -> 650ms. Still elevated but improving.

leah: Good. Initiate fallback to smaller model variant for heavy gen routes as temporary mitigation (reduce tail latency). Alex take point?

alex: On it — adding header-based model fallback for /v1/generate to use model=redwood-lite-v1 via edge rule. Patch deployed (edge-routes v12).

deploy-bot: edge-routes v12 deployed to eu-west (canary 10%). Rollout ID r-2026-778.

kevin: Customer impact note: 3 customers affected, rate ~2-5% per customer, degraded responses and occasional timeouts. CS notified and running incident template.

leah: Good. Samir, can you run a focused log search for 502 signatures and KV cache errors?

samir: Running query: `status:502 AND service:edge-mux* AND message:KVCache` — returns several matches on mux-7. Looks like a transient connection reset to upstream cache that correlates with spikes.

jordan: I see increased upstream TCP resets to cache cluster from mux-7 (netstat shows ESTABLISHED -> RST). Possible connection pool exhaustion during burst.

alex: Short-term mitigations checklist: 1) circuit off problem pods (done), 2) model fallback (canary in progress), 3) increase upstream keepalive and connection pool on muxes, 4) warm additional mux capacity.

leah: Jordan, please warm 2 standby mux pods and increase pool size by +20% (config change). Samir, track error trend. Kevin, keep AMs updated.

jordan: Warming 2 pods now. Patch to pool config in progress: `edge-config set mux_conn_pool 1.2x --env eu-west`

samir: Error rate now 1.9% and falling. p95 at 320ms. Looks like knockback + fallback + pool bump working.

leah: Marking incident as "mitigation in place". Continue monitoring for 30m. If stable, we'll move to postmortem. Can someone create INC ticket and link playbook?

kevin: Created INC ticket INC-2026-0427 in our tracker and assigned to triage team. Link: https://issues.redwood/INC-2026-0427

alex: I'll follow-up with a change to make model-fallback automatic on detection for short windows.

leah: Thank you team. Final notes for now: capture heap/profile from mux-7, export tcpdump slice (1m) around peak, retain logs for 72h. I'll post postmortem owner after stabilization. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0427 status updated: mitigation in place. Next update scheduled +10m.

kevin: CS update sent to impacted customers with ETA ~30-45m for resolution.

samir: Leaving minute-by-minute watch on metrics. Will ping if anything bounces back.

leah: Closing slack command room for now — stand by for postmortem. Thanks all. :pray:
